_comment: One job definition, reused for all seven shardable poster-metrics-pipeline scripts (01/02/03/04/05/10/11) -- same image as ecs/task-definition-metrics.json, same EFS mount, same reasoning as batch/job-definition.json: shards write to data/ on shared storage, the merge step afterward reads all of them from there. Higher memory than the validator's Batch job definition (3072 -> 8192) and 2 vCPU instead of 1 -- these seven scripts load real torch models (pyiqa, NIMA/InceptionV2, LAION's CLIP ViT-L/14 + MLP head, CLIP ViT-B/32, SigLIP-base) into memory per container, not just make boto3 calls. retryStrategy and resumability work exactly like the validator's: 01/02/03/04/05/10/11 already support --shard-index/--shard-count AND load_done_ids/open_for_append-style resume (or the ids-already-in-.npz check for 05/11), so a Batch-retried child re-reads its own --out first and only redoes ids it doesn't already have.
_gpu_note: This is a CPU-only (FARGATE) job definition, same platform choice as the validator's, for cost-safety continuity -- see docs/COST_SAFETY.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's note on why. All seven of these scripts run real neural-net inference (pyiqa/NIMA/LAION/CLIP/SigLIP) and would run meaningfully faster on a GPU-backed Batch compute environment (EC2 launch type, e.g. g4dn/g5 instances -- Fargate itself has no GPU support at all). If wall-clock time at full 145k-poster scale becomes the bottleneck, that's the documented next step, not something this design defaults to.
